national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that service should be the main purpose of life and must be inherent in every individual. He said that in politics too, service should remain the guiding principle, even when one reaches the highest position. Mr Modi made these remarks during a virtual interaction with Seva Yatris travelling on the Yatra from Vadnagar to Varanasi. The Prime Minister said, ‘Seva Paramo Dharma’ service is the highest duty should remain the guiding principle. Mr Modi said, service is the biggest driving force. He said, whether it is PM-KISAN or the PM Surya Ghar Yojana, countless such schemes are recognised for their last-mile delivery. The Prime Minister said, it is only when there is a spirit of service, four crore poor have receive permanent houses. He said, when the spirit of service is integrated into a nation’s policies, service itself becomes the greatest driving force for the country’s progress. Mr Modi said, it gives rise to innovative schemes that bring out 25 crore citizens from the cycle of poverty. He said, politics, elections, and systems of governance have their own place. The Prime Minister said, we are people dedicated to nation-building and set out with the resolve to build a developed India. He said, everyone must vigorously advance the pivotal role of the youth in building a developed India by 2047. Mr Modi said, today’s young generation is both the architect of a developed India and the one that will be a major beneficiary of it. During the interaction, Seva Yatris shared their experiences with the Prime Minister. They said that they planted saplings and conducted cleanliness drives as part of the campaign. They added that during the yatra, they interacted with people and received their positive feedback on the benefits of various government schemes.

national_raw_news.title: 49 mins ago | National 100 Govt reduces Basic Customs Duty on crude edible oils amid rising global prices
national_raw_news.content: The Government has reduced the Basic Customs Duty (BCD) on major imported crude edible oils with a view to moderating domestic edible oil prices. This provides relief to consumers and mitigates inflationary pressures arising from the sharp increase in international edible oil prices. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the BCD on Crude Sunflower Oil has been reduced from 10% to Nil, while the BCD on Crude Soybean Oil and Crude Palm Oil has been reduced from 10% to 5% It also said that the Government has simultaneously reduced the applicable BCD on the refined edible oils while maintaining an import duty differential of 19.25% between crude and refined edible oils. The Ministry informed that the reduction in BCD on crude edible oils is expected to lower their landed cost and facilitate transmission of the benefit through the domestic supply chain. It said that the measure is intended to provide relief to consumers while contributing to the broader objective of containing food-price and overall inflationary pressures. The Government has also issued an advisory to edible oil associations and industry stakeholders to ensure that the full benefit arising from the reduction in import duty is passed on to consumers. Government, in a statement, said that Industry stakeholders have been requested to immediately revise their Price to Distributors and Maximum Retail Price in accordance with the reduction in landed costs. Edible oil associations have also been requested to advise their members to implement the corresponding price reductions without delay.

national_raw_news.title: 51 mins ago | Sports 17 Asian Games: India wins silver medals in mixed relay race and Wushu; Seema Kumari bags historic B...
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian Games, 2026 Indian runners have clinched silver in the mixed 4x400m relay race at Nagoya today. The quartet of Poovamma Raju, Vishal Thennarasu, Vithya Ramraj and Manu TS timed the run at 3 mins 14.46 seconds to defend India’s silver medal won in the last edition of the games in Hangzhou. Bahrain won the gold with Games record of 3 mins 12.87 seconds. Before that, Seema Kumari won bronze in the 10,000 metre race after finishing at third spot in 32.50 mins. The achievement marks India’s first medal in the women’s 10,000m event at the Asian Games in 16 years. Earlier, in Shooting, Anant Jeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal also bagged bronze in the mixed skeet team event, the first-ever medal for India in this category. The Indian pair missed just four of 48 shots and finished level with South Korea, but lost to South Korea in the tie-breaker. China won Gold. In Boxing, Parveen made it to the quarterfinals of the Women’s 65kg category after receiving a walkover from Tajikistan’s Malika Nozimova in the round of 16 at Nishio. She will now face reigning world silver medallist Navbakhor Khamidova of Uzbekistan. In the morning, Indian wushu player Roshibina Devi Naorem won Silver in the Women’s 60kg Sanda event after losing 0-2 to China’s Zhang Xiaoyu in the final. It was third Asian Games medal for Roshibina, after Silver 2023 Hangzhou Games and Bronze in 2018 Jakarta-Palembang Games. In Men’s double sculls rowing, Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won bronze. However, Commonwealth Games champion Sakshi Chaudhary bowed out of the Games after her loss in the Women’s 51 kg pre-quarters to reigning World Champion Alua Balkibekova. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated medal winning players.

national_raw_news.title: IRDAI proposes overhaul of insurance distribution framework 4 hours ago 183
national_raw_news.content: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed a major overhaul of the insurance distribution framework, including a simpler three-tier architecture, lower expense limits, revamped commission structures and stronger safeguards against mis-selling. The insurance regulator released a public consultation paper on “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution”, outlining reforms covering distribution structure, expenses, commissions, market conduct, transparency and the use of digital infrastructure. Under the proposed norms, insurers and large distribution entities will have to disclose their commission policies and structures in a simple and accessible manner. Specified commercial policies will also carry commission disclosures, enabling customers to be aware of the distribution costs built into the pricing. The consultation paper also proposes tighter measures to curb mis-selling and compulsory bundling of insurance with other financial products. These include documenting customer needs and suitability, bringing direct and indirect remuneration within the regulatory definition of commission, and prohibiting volume-linked or reward-linked incentives for bank and Non-Banking Financial Company staff selling insurance. IRDAI has further proposed linking the identity of the individual seller with each policy, placing information on mis-selling incidents in the public domain and allowing commission claw-backs in cases of mis-selling. A key part of the proposed reforms is a reduction in insurers’ Expense of Management (EoM) limits. For life insurers, the EoM limit would shift to a company-level basis linked to Gross Direct Premium Income (GDPI), with the ceiling proposed at 15 per cent within two years and 12.5 per cent within five years. For general insurers, the calculation would shift from Gross Written Premium (GWP) to domestic GDPI, while the EoM limit would progressively decline from 30 per cent of GWP to 20 per cent of GDPI within five years.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram launches first ‘Pluck & Pay’ festival to boost rural tourism 8 hours ago 124
national_raw_news.content: Mizoram has launched its first ‘Pluck & Pay’ festival in Khawzawl district in the eastern part of the state, offering visitors an opportunity to harvest farm produce themselves and pay farmers directly as the state seeks to expand tourism-led livelihood opportunities in rural communities, officials said. The three-day festival, being held from September 23 to 25 at Tualte and Chawngtlai villages, has been jointly organised by the state Tourism department and the office of the Khawzawl Deputy Commissioner. The initiative brings agriculture, horticulture, tourism, local food and community enterprise together, allowing visitors to experience rural life while creating direct economic linkages with farming households, officials said. Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said the initiative reflected the state’s broader vision of ensuring that tourism benefits the communities hosting visitors. “The future of tourism is not only about taking visitors to places; it is about creating value for the people who make those places worth visiting,” he said, adding that the government wanted stronger linkages between tourism and villages, farms, entrepreneurs and cultural communities. Besides farm visits and harvesting, the festival features traditional Mizo music and dance, local cuisine, handicrafts, cultural performances and traditional recreational games, besides visits to historical and tourist sites. The initiative is aimed at creating an ecosystem in which tourism spending can also support local farmers, homestays, guides, transport operators, artisans and other community-based enterprises. The launch marks the beginning of Mizoram’s 2026 festival season, with the Anthurium Festival at Reiek, Hnahsin Kût in Champhai and Travel Fest in Aizawl among the events lined up in the coming months. Leitlangpui Music Festival, Winter Festival, Tlaizawng Paradise Festival and Sakawrhmuituai Sunset Event are also scheduled as part of the wider tourism calendar. Official figures presented during the recent state assembly session showed tourist arrivals rising from 4,27,302 in 2024 to 8,41,322 in 2025. The ‘Pluck & Pay’ initiative seeks to leverage this growing visitor base to increase the participation of rural communities in the state’s tourism economy, officials added.
